To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the in vivo water reference method provides the most accurate and precise estimates of metabolite concentrations, (2) the water signal is a suitable reference for quantification of in vivo proton spectra of the brain and of the liver, and (3) the water reference method can be applied with high accuracy in vivo.

the water signal is a suitable internal reference for the quantification of in vivo proton MR spectra; that the in vivo water resonance is a single peak; that the water peak is not affected by the presence of lipids; that the in vitro water resonance can be used to calibrate the in vivo water peak; that the in situ water resonance can be measured in vivo and that the in situ and in vitro water resonances are identical.

the in vivo water resonance is a reliable internal reference, that it is possible to obtain quantitative estimates of the concentration of the major metabolites in vivo with a precision better than 10%, and that it is possible in vivo to measure the concentration of metabolites that are present in the millimolar range.
